article_title: Valkey 9.2.0 Reaches General Availability as a Coordinated Patch Fixes a Client-Eviction Use-After-Free Across Five Other Branches
summary: Automated checks passed; manual review found two recoverable issues: three quoted phrases attributed to the GHSA advisory paraphrase rather than reproduce its text verbatim, and a false absence claim that the advisory does not name a reporter (it does).

findings.message: Three direct quotes in the 'What We Know' section, all attributed to the GHSA-3885-pq5f-788j advisory (source-1), paraphrase the advisory's wording rather than reproducing it verbatim.
findings.details: Article: "replies sent to blocked clients push client memory over the threshold, causing the system to evict the client whose command initiated the unblock operation while that client is still active on the call stack" / "results in reliable server crashes" / "systems with maxmemory-clients 0 (default setting) remain unaffected". Advisory's actual text: "If the replies sent to blocked clients earlier in the same pass push client memory over maxmemory-clients, evictClients() can pick the client whose command made the key ready, which is still on the call stack... The result is a reliable crash of the server process. Servers with maxmemory-clients 0 (the default) are not affected." Each quote has real textual basis in the source (not fabricated from nothing) but none is verbatim; quote 1 also subtly shifts the source's possibility framing ('can pick') to a causal certainty framing ('causing...to evict'). Confined to a subordinate paragraph, not the headline/summary/lead.

findings.message: The 'What We Don't Know' section states the GHSA advisory 'does not name a reporter,' which is false — the advisory's Credits section names one.
findings.details: Source-1 (GHSA-3885-pq5f-788j) states verbatim: "Credits The defect was found and fixed by https://github.com/nadav-levanoni (issue #5422, fix #5435)." The advisory does not state whether the discovery method was an AI-assisted audit or conventional testing, so the article's underlying speculative question is still open, but the specific claim that the advisory omits a reporter's name is incorrect.

content_preview.title: Valkey 9.2.0 Reaches General Availability as a Coordinated Patch Fixes a Client-Eviction Use-After-Free Across Five Other Branches
content_preview.summary: Valkey shipped 9.2.0 and five security-only updates on the same day, fixing a client-eviction use-after-free tracked as CVE-2026-130822.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Valkey 9.2.0, the first stable release of the project's 9.2 series, became generally available on November 18, 2026, according to the [Valkey GitHub release notes](https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey/releases/tag/9.2.0). The same day, the project shipped security-only updates for five older branches — 9.1.4, 9.0.8, 8.1.12, 8.0.13, and 7.2.16 — fixing a client-eviction use-after-free flaw tracked as [CVE-2026-130822](https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey/security/advisories/GHSA-3885-p...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured News piece. Overview states the GA date and the coordinated six-branch security patch; What We Know separates the vulnerability mechanism, the patch rollout, and the new 9.2.0 features; What We Don't Know is appropriately scoped. No sensationalism, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 7 sources snapshotted successfully (status 200, no suspicious_patterns), sha256-verified against manifest.json, and read in full from the decompressed .html.gz files (not re-fetched live). source-0 (github.com/valkey-io/valkey/releases/tag/9.2.0): confirms 'Released Wed 18 November 2026', CVE-2026-130822/use-after-free fix framing, and the Path Hash 'exact lookup, longest-prefix matching, and prefix traversal over binary-safe paths' quote verbatim. source-1 (GHSA-3885-pq5f-788j advisory): confirms CVE ID, CWE-416, CVSS 7.5 / CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H vector verbatim, and the underlying bug mechanism and mitigation — but the article's three quoted phrases describing the mechanism paraphrase rather than reproduce this source's wording (see findings), and the article's 'does not name a reporter' claim is false — the advisory's Credits section names github.com/nadav-levanoni as the finder/fixer. source-2 (9.1.4 release notes): confirms 'a use-after-free crash in client eviction when maxmemory-clients is enabled' and 'Upgrade urgency SECURITY' verbatim. source-3 (7.2.16 release notes): same two quotes confirmed verbatim. source-4 (releases page): confirms all six branches (9.2.0, 9.1.4, 9.0.8, 8.1.12, 8.0.13, 7.2.16) show 'Released Wed 18 November 2026' and all five older branches carry the identical CVE-2026-130822 use-after-free fix entry, substantiating the 'same day, six branches' claim even for the three branches (9.0.8, 8.1.12, 8.0.13) not individually cited by their own release-note URLs. source-5 (valkey.io 9.2 blog): confirms the ACL-roles quote, the 36-43% memory overhead figure, and the 52% replication-bandwidth figure verbatim, plus forkless snapshots, Zstandard, and hot-key-detection feature claims factually. source-6 (valkey.io AI-security blog, Sept 17 2026): confirms all five quotes in that paragraph verbatim (advisory counts, AI-cost framing, 'running AI-driven adversarial audits', '34 real bugs').
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline, summary, and lead (Overview) are fully supported: GA date, CVE number, six affected branches, and the link characterizing the September RC as a precursor are all verified against the cited sources. The two issues found (quote fidelity in the mechanism description; the false 'no reporter named' claim) are both confined to subordinate sentences in the body, not the headline/summary/lead, and are addressed in a corrections record rather than blocking publication.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. No loaded language; attributes claims to 'the advisory', 'the project's blog', 'the release notes' rather than stating them as established fact.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. The Herald's September 23, 2026 article (2026-09/23-valkey-92-release-candidate-...) covered the 9.2.0-rc1 release candidate and a different security fix (a SORT/ACL bypass). This submission covers the final GA release six weeks later plus a newly disclosed, distinct vulnerability (CVE-2026-130822, a client-eviction use-after-free) patched across six branches simultaneously — genuine new news, not a rewrite. Confirmed via grep that no prior published article mentions CVE-2026-130822, and no other November 2026 article covers the Valkey 9.2.0 GA release.
editor_notes.quote_audit: Every string inside double quotes in body_markdown (14 total) was extracted and checked character-for-character against the cited snapshot's plain-text extraction. 11 of 14 are exact verbatim matches (quotes 4-14, spanning source-2, source-3, source-0, source-5, and source-6). 3 of 14 (quotes 1-3, all attributed to source-1, the GHSA advisory, in a single paragraph describing the vulnerability mechanism) are paraphrases dressed as verbatim quotes — each has real textual basis in the source but none reproduces it exactly, and quote 1 subtly reframes the source's possibility language ('can pick') as causal certainty ('causing...to evict'). No quote was found to be fully fabricated with zero basis in any source, and no quote was found misattributed to the wrong source (contrast with the sibling PR #2944 rejection, which had a fully fabricated quote plus a wrong-source citation across 5 total failures spanning 4 sources). This submission's quote-fidelity problem is narrower: 3 related paraphrase-as-quote instances from one source about one fact, confined to a subordinate paragraph — recoverable with a single corrections entry rather than requiring rejection.
editor_notes.anthropic_disclosure: Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article is about Valkey/Redis-family database releases; Anthropic and Claude are not the subject, and no Anthropic/Claude credit line appears.
editor_notes.allowlist_check: All cited hosts (github.com, valkey.io) are already present in config/source_allowlist.txt. No allowlist additions needed.
concerns: Three quotes in the 'What We Know' vulnerability-mechanism paragraph paraphrase the GHSA advisory rather than reproducing it verbatim (see findings/quote_audit).
The 'What We Don't Know' section's claim that the advisory 'does not name a reporter' is false; the advisory credits github.com/nadav-levanoni as finder/fixer.
recommendations: Future submissions: check every string inside quotation marks character-for-character against the cited snapshot before submission, and verify absence/negative claims ('does not name X') against the full source text, not just the sections most relevant to the article's framing.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate and well-sourced News coverage of a genuine, distinct GA release and security patch, with the headline/summary/lead fully verified against primary sources. Two recoverable subordinate issues (paraphrased quotes presented as verbatim; a false claim that the advisory omits a reporter's name) are documented in a corrections record rather than blocking publication, since neither affects the headline, summary, or lead and a single corrections note can honestly inform readers of both. Featured candidacy: 0 - routine coordinated point-release and security-patch coverage for a defined developer/ops audience, not exceptional or broadly newsworthy.
